file_format: one JSON document: a list of entry objects separated by commas (or {"entries": [...]}); bare objects one after another (JSON Lines) are refused; at most 500 entries

meaning.rejected_alternatives: what was considered and not chosen ('none' is an answer, empty is not)

gap.title_convention: <Section>: no evidence yet — the form that marks a PRODUCT or TECH section as explained (need_gap)

values.text: every field is text, except sources and the list fields below

lists.rejected_alternatives: text, or a list of texts (written joined with '; ')

values.title: one line, at most 200 characters, without '**' or '|'
values.over_a_limit: refused, never cut: split the entry
values.never: an HTML comment marker (<!--, -->) in any field

sources.<path>, <path>#heading, <path>:line or <: a tracked file of a repo this brain owns
sources.<repo>:<path>: the same, when the brain owns several repos
sources.file:<absolute path>: an existing, non-secret file (a document the person gave)
sources.user: the person's own answer (the only source that is not outside content)

knowledge_standard: Keep a unit only if all three hold: it is useful in another task; a capable person who was not here would go wrong or waste time without it; you can point to its evidence.

Write each unit as situation (applicability: a recognisable trigger, not "when developing"), judgment (what; how for a process), reason (why; for a decision also rejected_alternatives) and evidence. It must stand on its own for a reader who was not here: no "above", "this" or "plan A".
The state of the moment (not pushed, needs a build, not verified yet, a count that will change) is not knowledge and is not written into any unit.
What one look at the code or the data answers (a signature, a schema, a constant's value, a file's layout) is no lesson.
A problem still open is a gap, never a lesson.
Commit hashes, run ids, version numbers of a document and approval dates are evidence, not knowledge: they stay out of a unit's text.

sections.take_from: what the material says the project is for: the README's positioning, the package description
comparisons with alternatives the material itself makes ("unlike X, ...")
what the material calls a priority, a goal or the order of what comes first
sections.not: a design choice kept for compatibility (Architecture or Recent Decisions) or a rule for changes (Conventions); none stated: a gap

sections.take_from: what the material says counts as success: a target, a measure, a definition of done for the project
sections.not: a test, review or install step for contributors or users (Conventions); none stated: a gap

sections.take_from: what the material says is out of scope or not to be used for
sections.not: anything the material does not say is out of scope; none stated: a gap

sections.take_from: ARCHITECTURE and design documents; the entry points

one per code_shape.graph_clusters cluster that matters: responsibility, entry point, what it depends on; sources = the cluster's files (never a graph id). When graph_clusters.skipped says the graph was too large to cluster: one per module in code_shape.structure.modules that matters (leave out test modules), what it depends on from structure.module_edges, the repo's own architecture or key-files index for the responsibility; sources = files from the module's files (a directory is not a source)
CONTRIBUTING and the conventions configs; one process per dev command (how = the command, sources = the CI, Makefile or package.json that declares it)
each history.hotspots file not marked test, with its commit subjects: the trap it shows; security and bugfix CHANGELOG entries; SECURITY.md
sections.not: the hot-spot list itself or which files change most (it changes with every commit)

sections.take_from: reverts and repeated fixes, citing the commits' files
gaps only: what has no evidence (untested entry points, a document that disagrees with the code, an empty PRODUCT or TECH section)
accepted ADRs and design-document decisions, with why and rejected_alternatives
sections.not: a rejected or proposed ADR presented as decided

good: [pitfall] Changing the default digest invalidates every issued token. Applies when upgrading or configuring the digest (a trigger, a consequence, a source)
bad: [model] Uses Python (a fact any file listing shows)
a version number, a count, "currently working on ...", anything no source supports

refusals.shape: a field, type, section or length, or the file's format: fix the entries file and run bootstrap-apply again
refusals.evidence: a source that points at nothing this brain may cite: cite a real one, or drop the claim
refusals.doc: the doc already holds the person's own writing: nothing was added; show them the entry and ask (never edit the entries file for it)
refusals.state: the brain is not setting up: bootstrap writes only a newborn brain

repos.note: this brain owns no repo: cite file:, url: or user
